guesses.reason: Short, dense coat in solid blue-gray with a white blaze, muzzle, chest and belly is the classic random-bred bicolor pattern.
The even blue-gray color and green eyes hint at Russian Blue, but the white markings and build point to a mix.
The large amount of white on the body could suggest some Van-pattern influence, though the coat and face are typical of a domestic cat.

breed.appearance: A slender, medium-sized shorthaired cat with a solid blue-gray coat over the head, ears, shoulders and back patches, and bright white on the muzzle, chin, chest, belly and legs; an inverted-V white blaze runs up between the eyes to the forehead. Large upright triangular ears are gray with pale inner fur, and the round eyes are yellow-green with vertical pupils. The nose leather is dusky gray-pink with a small gray smudge beside it, the whiskers are long and white, and the white front paw shows a few dark gray toe pads.
breed.fun_fact: Gray-and-white bicolor cats like Buddy come in endless one-of-a-kind patterns, so no two look exactly alike!
